# Recipient, authority and account-reference matrix

Each row identifies one person with a double-barrelled surname and the records that person may inspect. A common component in two surnames does not establish that the rows concern the same individual or permit their contact details to be exchanged.

| Person | Capacity | Contact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ⟦PERSON|Ailsa Quennell-Rusk⟧ | Recipient | ⟦EMAIL|ailsa.records@quennell-rill.invalid⟧; ⟦PHONE|+44 7700 900528⟧ |
| ⟦PERSON|Nerovan MacVell-Rusk⟧ | Attorney | ⟦EMAIL|nerovan.review@macvell-purl.invalid⟧; ⟦PHONE|+44 7700 900639⟧ |

| Scheduled records | Account | Authority reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Equipment receipts | ⟦BANK|GB63 QUEN 4038 2719 6504 82⟧ | Paragraph 3.1 |
| Storage receipts | ⟦BANK|GB28 VELL 2074 9163 5802 44⟧ | Paragraph 3.2 |

The reference in the final column identifies the relevant paragraph of the signed authority. It is not a personal or case identifier. The account value identifies the record set and does not itself authorise a payment.

The attorney named in the second row may prepare a comparison for the recipient named in the first row. Any proposed change to the recipient or the account schedule requires a signed amendment before release of an original record.

The approved inspection date is 28 February 2027. The charge is GBP 48. Each original instruction must be retained with the corresponding table and any later explanation of a correction.
